newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rose in week -- FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rose in week -- FHLMC.

text.p: The average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages rose three basis points in the week ending January 31 from the previous week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said on Thursday.
The 30-year interest rate inched up to an average 7.88 percent from 7.85 percent last week, while the 15-year rose to 7.38 percent from 7.35 percent, Freddie Mac said.
But one-year adjustable-rate mortgages inched down to an average 5.55 percent from 5.57 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.02 percent, the 15-year 6.52 percent and the ARM 5.37 percent.

"Steady interest rates are a reflection of the general consensus that the economy is not expanding too quickly, therefore the Federal Reserve Board will most probably not make any moves to raise rates when it meets next Tuesday," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"Comparatively low mortgage rates and low inflation combine to help make this a very affordable time for those who are planning to invest in a home," Van Order added.
On Friday the Commerce Department will issue U.S. December single-family home sales data. The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on February 4 and 5.
Last Monday the National Association of Realtors reported that sales of U.S. December existing homes fell 3.5 percent to a 3.87 million unit annual rate.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.7 percent on the 15-year, down from 1.8 percent last week, and 1.4 percent on the ARM, unchanged from last week.
